blocks.text: Explains the central design rule (anything uncertain → unknown → ask, never allow), lists every shell construct the scanner handles, and separately lists every construct it marks unknown. Also states the complexity bounds and that the module is pure (standard library, no I/O, no logging).
blocks.title: Module docstring: scope, what is understood, and what is marked unknown

blocks.text: MAX_LENGTH, MAX_DEPTH, MAX_PARTS, and _MAX_WORK bound the input and work. _REDUCERS are keywords whose following command is still parsed. _KEYWORDS are reserved words that cannot be analysed at all. _OPAQUE is the list of programs (ssh, docker, watch, etc.) whose arguments the parser does not model, so they are always marked unknown.
blocks.title: Global constants and opaque-program lists

blocks.text: Four frozen dataclasses form the public API. Word carries the dequoted text plus three flags (expands, glob, quoted) and is_assign. Redirect stores the operator, the optional fd, and the target Word. Part is one simple command: argv, assigns, redirects, unknown reasons, an optional wrapper name, and the chain of dissolved neutral wrappers in via. ParseResult aggregates Parts and top-level unknown reasons.
blocks.title: Result types: Word, Redirect, Part, ParseResult

blocks.text: __init__ sets up all mutable state: position, word/assign/redirect accumulators, the group stack, heredoc queue, budget, and unknown lists. run() increments the work budget, rejects control characters, then scans character by character dispatching to helpers for whitespace, comment, separator, grouping, redirection, and word. At EOF it checks for dangling state (unmatched groups, pending redirections, open heredocs) and adds unknown reasons for each.
blocks.title: _Parser initialisation and main scan loop

blocks.text: _add_word decides what to do with each completed word. If a redirect is pending (self.pending), the word becomes its target; heredoc operators cause a here-document unknown to be recorded. At command-start a bare '{' or '}' opens or closes a brace group. Leading NAME=value words before the first non-assignment go to assigns; everything else goes to argv. _flush() is called by separators and EOF: it strips leading '!' and reducer keywords, calls _peel_assignments, then delegates to _classify.
blocks.title: Word routing: redirect targets, assignments, and command argv

blocks.anchor: def _classify(self, argv, assigns, redirs, unknown, via) -> None:
blocks.text: Dispatches on the base name of argv[0]. A non-literal command word is immediately unknown. Keywords go to _emit with 'shell keyword'. eval and source get their own unknown reasons. Neutral wrappers (time, nohup, etc.) are stripped by _neutral and the inner argv is re-classified with the wrapper added to via. Shell (sh, bash, …), su, env, sudo/doas/pkexec, xargs, and find each have a dedicated handler that emits the wrapper Part and then recurses for the wrapped command. _OPAQUE programs emit 'runs another program'. Everything else emits a plain Part.
blocks.title: Command classification and wrapper handling

blocks.anchor: def _shell(self, name, argv, rest, plain) -> None:
blocks.text: _shell parses 'sh -c STRING': options before and after -c are accepted, the first non-option word is the command string, which is then re-parsed via _wrapped_string. _privilege (sudo/doas/pkexec) and _env strip their flags with _skip_options before recursing. _xargs emits the wrapper and the wrapped argv with 'arguments are supplied at run time'. _find emits the find itself and then processes each -exec/-execdir clause as a wrapped argv.
blocks.title: Wrapper handlers: shell, su, env, privilege, xargs, find

blocks.text: Checks that command is a string within MAX_LENGTH and without NUL, then runs _Parser and converts its parts and deduplicated unknowns into a ParseResult. Any exception (RecursionError, MemoryError, or a parser bug) is caught and returned as ParseResult((), ('parser failure',)).
blocks.title: Public entry point

gotchas: parse() never raises — it catches Exception at the outermost level and returns a 'parser failure' result
unknown reasons are fixed strings (never the command text), because ParseResult is shown to users
Consecutive '**' in a glob pattern and many other shell constructs are intentionally marked unknown rather than guessed
The _Budget caps total characters parsed across all nesting (_MAX_WORK = 8 × MAX_LENGTH) to prevent exponential blowup in deeply nested substitutions
Neutral wrappers (time, nohup, etc.) are dissolved only when they appear without a leading '/' — 'time' is neutral, '/usr/bin/time' is treated as a plain command
how_it_works: parse() wraps a _Parser run in a try/except so any bug produces a fail-closed unknown result instead of a crash
_Parser.run() scans the command character by character, calling helpers for separators, redirections, grouping, and words; each complete simple command is flushed via _flush() → _classify()
_classify() identifies wrappers (neutral ones are dissolved by recursing through _classify; authority-raising ones like sh, sudo, env emit two parts: the wrapper and the wrapped command)
Words are assembled by _WordBuilder, which tracks whether each word is a pure literal, contains an expansion, or contains a glob — a non-literal command word is unknown
Command substitutions $(…) and backticks are parsed recursively via _sub(), contributing their commands as parts that run before the containing command; nesting is capped at MAX_DEPTH
inputs: command: any object (non-string returns a ParseResult with an unknown reason)
outputs: ParseResult: tuple of Part objects in execution order, plus top-level unknown reasons
purpose: The policy engine needs to know which commands a shell string runs so it can apply allow/ask/deny rules to each one. This module parses the subset of shell syntax that can be classified with certainty and labels everything else as unknown, which the engine turns into 'ask'. It never raises and is linear in input length. Standard library only, no I/O.
summary: Hand-written shell tokeniser for the m2c policy engine: produces a list of simple commands from an arbitrary shell string, marking everything uncertain as unknown.

symbols.summary: Frozen dataclass representing one shell word after dequoting, with flags for expansions, globs, quoting, and assignment form.
True when the word contains no variable expansion and no glob, meaning its value is known at parse time.
Frozen dataclass holding one shell redirection: the operator string, an optional file descriptor, and the target Word.

symbols.details: For >& the target is treated as a file descriptor dup if it is a literal ASCII digit or '-'; anything else is treated as a file write.
symbols.summary: Returns True when this redirection operator probably creates or truncates a file (>, >>, >|, <>, &>, &>> and >& not to a literal fd).
Returns True when this redirection opens a file for reading (< and <> unconditionally; <& only when the target is not a literal digit or '-').
Frozen dataclass for one simple command: its argument words, leading assignments, redirections, unknown reasons, wrapper name, and dissolved-wrapper chain.
Returns the raw text of argv[0], or None if the command has no argument words.
Returns the base name of the command word (last path segment), or None if argv is empty.
Returns the argv words joined by spaces, excluding leading assignments.
Returns assignments followed by argv words joined by spaces — the full original command including variable prefixes.
Frozen dataclass: the top-level result of parse(), holding all extracted Parts and any top-level unknown reasons.
True when neither the top-level result nor any individual Part has an unknown reason — meaning the parse is fully classified.
Returns the deduplicated union of all unknown reasons from the top level and from every Part, in first-seen order.

symbols.details: Uses an explicit character set rather than str.isdigit() because isdigit() accepts Unicode superscripts and other numeric forms that bash treats as file names, not file descriptor numbers.
symbols.summary: Returns True iff t is a non-empty string consisting entirely of ASCII digit characters 0–9.

symbols.summary: Finds the matching '}' for a '${' by counting only '{' and '}' (quotes are handled by the caller); returns the index or -1.

symbols.returns: str with one layer of backslash escaping removed
symbols.summary: Strips the extra layer of backslash escaping from the body of a backtick substitution before it is re-parsed.
Accumulates characters and flags while scanning one shell word, then produces a Word via build().
Initialises all accumulator state: empty buffer, all flags False, plain=True (every character so far fits a NAME), eq=None.

symbols.details: Tracks whether the word so far is a valid NAME=value assignment: NAME chars are allowed; '=' at a non-initial position sets eq to record an assignment; '+=' prefix is recognised. Any other character clears the plain flag and ends assignment detection.

params.desc: the following character (used to detect '+=' sequences)
params.name: nxt

symbols.summary: Appends a plain (unquoted) character and updates the glob, brace, and assignment-detection flags.
Finalises the accumulated buffer into a Word, treating brace expressions as expansions (unless bare '{' or '}') and single '[' as not a glob.
Shared mutable counter that tracks the total number of Parts emitted and total characters processed across all nested _Parser instances, enforcing MAX_PARTS and _MAX_WORK.
Hand-written recursive-descent scanner that converts a shell command string into Parts and unknown reasons.

params.desc: current nesting depth (0 at the top level)
params.name: depth

params.desc: shared Budget counting parts and work across all nesting levels
params.name: budget

symbols.summary: Initialises the parser for one string at a given nesting depth, sharing the Budget with its parent.
Appends a Part to the results list, capping at MAX_PARTS and recording 'too many commands' once if the cap is exceeded.

symbols.details: Increments budget.work by len(s) and returns early if _MAX_WORK is exceeded. Rejects control characters (ASCII < 32 except tab and newline) with an unknown reason. After the loop, records unknowns for a dangling redirect target, unmatched groups, or open heredocs.
symbols.summary: Main scan loop: consumes the input character by character, dispatching to sub-methods for each token type, then checks for unclosed groups and pending redirections at EOF.
Returns True when no words, assignments, redirections, or pending redirections have been accumulated for the current command.
Handles a '(' character: opens a subshell group if at command start; records 'arithmetic command' for '((' and 'unexpected (' mid-command.
Closes a subshell '(' or brace group '{': flushes any accumulated command, pops the group stack, and records 'empty or incomplete group' when nothing was between the delimiters.

params.desc: the separator string that caused the flush (e.g. ';', '&&', 'newline', 'eof')
params.name: op

symbols.summary: Handles a command separator (;, &&, ||, |, &, newline, eof): flushes the current command if anything was accumulated, records 'empty command' or 'incomplete command' for dangling operators.

symbols.details: If self.pending is set, the word becomes the redirect target (and heredoc operators record a here-document unknown). At command start, bare '{' and '}' open and close brace groups respectively. A leading assignment word goes to assigns; all others go to argv.
symbols.summary: Routes a completed Word to its destination: redirect target, brace-group open/close, assignment list, or argv.
Finalises the current command: strips leading '!' and reducer keywords, peels remaining assignments, then delegates to _classify.

params.desc: remaining argument words after wrapper removal
params.name: words

symbols.returns: (words, assigns) with leading assignment words moved
symbols.summary: Moves leading unquoted NAME=value words from the front of words into assigns, for contexts where a wrapper (time, !) has already been stripped.

symbols.details: For process substitution, _find_close locates the matching ')' and the inner text is parsed via _sub; the whole construct is added as an expansion word. Otherwise, the longest matching operator from _REDIR_OPS is consumed; if the last accumulated word is a bare digit immediately before the operator it is stolen as the fd.
symbols.summary: Handles '<' or '>' at the current position: detects process substitution <(…) / >(…) and processes it, or matches the redirect operator and sets up a pending redirect.
Consumes pending heredoc bodies from the input after a newline: scans line by line until each delimiter is found and, for unquoted delimiters, parses any command substitutions in the body.
Scans one shell word from the current position using _WordBuilder, handling backslash escapes, single quotes, double quotes, backticks, and '$' expansions.
Consumes a double-quoted string from the current position, feeding backslash escapes, '$' expansions, and backtick substitutions into the _WordBuilder.

params.desc: True when inside a double-quoted string (affects backslash escape rules)
params.name: in_dq

symbols.summary: Processes a backtick command substitution: finds the closing backtick, adds the expansion to the word builder, and parses the inner text as a sub-command.

symbols.details: For $(): calls _find_close and _sub on the body. For ${}: calls _find_brace_close; marks complex bodies (quotes, nested $()) unknown. For $((): marks arithmetic expansion unknown. For $': uses _find_ansi_quote. For plain $NAME: extends to the end of the name chars. Unknown/bare '$' is treated as literal.

params.desc: True when inside a double-quoted string
params.name: in_dq

symbols.summary: Dispatches on the character after '$': command substitution $(), parameter expansion ${}, arithmetic $(( / $[, $'...' ANSI string, plain variable $NAME, or special parameter $@/$?/etc.

params.desc: text to scan for nested substitutions (e.g. a ${...} body or a heredoc body)
params.name: text

symbols.summary: Scans arbitrary text for $(...) and backtick substitutions without regard to quoting (over-finds rather than under-finds) and parses each one via _sub.

params.name: inner

params.desc: unused keyword argument kept for signature symmetry
params.name: wrapped

symbols.details: Accepts '--' to end option processing. Short options are matched character by character against 'flags' (flag-only) and 'with_arg' (takes a following word). Long options are matched against long_flags (no arg), long_arg (separate arg), and long_eq (--key=value form). Returns None for any non-literal word or unrecognised option.

params.desc: string of single-letter options that take no argument
params.name: flags

params.desc: string of single-letter options that consume the next word
params.name: with_arg

params.desc: tuple of long options with no argument
params.name: long_flags

params.desc: tuple of long option prefixes that accept --key=value form
params.name: long_eq

params.desc: tuple of long options that take a separate following word
params.name: long_arg

symbols.returns: list of remaining Words after the options, or None if an unrecognised or non-literal option is found
symbols.summary: Consumes known option words from the front of a word list, returning the remaining positional words or None if an unrecognised option is encountered.

Strips the recognised options from a neutral wrapper (time, nohup, nice, ionice, setsid, stdbuf, timeout, builtin, command) and returns the remaining argv for re-classification, or None if the options are not understood.

symbols.details: Options may appear before and after -c (e.g. 'bash -c -x STRING'). The first non-option word after -c is the command string. A shell without -c (runs a script or stdin) is marked unknown. An unrecognised option or a non-literal string is also marked unknown.

params.desc: full argument list including the shell name
params.name: argv

params.desc: closure that creates a Part from the current context, optionally with extra unknown or wrapper
params.name: plain

symbols.summary: Handles 'sh -c STRING' and similar: parses shell flags before and after -c, extracts the literal command string, emits a wrapper Part, then re-parses the string via _wrapped_string.
Handles 'su -c STRING': scans for the -c flag followed by a literal string and re-parses it; emits 'su without a command string' if not found.
Handles the 'env' command: rejects --chdir/-C (directory change), strips known env flags, peels NAME=value assignments, then classifies the wrapped command.
Handles privilege-escalation wrappers (sudo, doas, pkexec): rejects --chdir/-D for sudo, strips known flags with _skip_options, then emits the wrapper and classifies the wrapped command.
Handles 'xargs': strips known flags, emits the wrapper Part, then classifies the wrapped argv with 'arguments are supplied at run time' as an extra unknown reason.
Handles 'find': emits the find Part, then processes each -exec/-execdir/-ok/-okdir clause as a wrapped argv terminated by ';' or '+'.

symbols.details: Returns immediately with a reason in unknown for non-string input, strings over MAX_LENGTH, or strings containing NUL. Any exception from _Parser (bug, RecursionError, MemoryError) is caught and returned as ParseResult((), ('parser failure',)).

params.desc: the shell command string to parse; non-strings are accepted and return a type-error unknown
params.name: command

symbols.returns: ParseResult with all extracted Parts and deduplicated unknown reasons
symbols.summary: Public entry point: parses a shell command string and returns a ParseResult; never raises regardless of input.
